The '''2017 Copa Libertadores finals''' were the two-legged final that decided the winner of the [[2017 Copa Libertadores|2017 Copa Libertadores de América]], the 58th edition of the [[Copa Libertadores|Copa Libertadores de América]], [[South America]]'s premier international club [[association football|football]] tournament organized by [[CONMEBOL]].

The finals were contested in two-legged home-and-away format between [[Brazilian Football Confederation|Brazilian]] team [[Grêmio Foot-Ball Porto Alegrense|Grêmio]] and [[Argentine Football Association|Argentinian]] team [[Club Atlético Lanús|Lanús]]. The first leg was hosted by Grêmio at [[Arena do Grêmio]] in [[Porto Alegre]] on 22 November 2017, while the second leg was hosted by Lanús at [[Estadio Ciudad de Lanús – Néstor Díaz Pérez|Estadio Ciudad de Lanús]] in [[Lanús]] on 29 November 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/es/definidos-fechas-y-horarios-de-los-partidos-finales |title=Definidos fechas y horarios de los partidos finales |publisher=CONMEBOL.com |language=es |date=3 November 2017}}</ref>  

Starting this season, the final matches was held again in November, 35 years since the previous November finals,  [[1982 Copa Libertadores finals|in 1982]]. 

The winners of the 2017 Copa Libertadores qualified as the CONMEBOL representative at the [[2017 FIFA Club World Cup]] in the United Arab Emirates, and also earned the right to play against the winners of the [[2017 Copa Sudamericana]] in the [[2018 Recopa Sudamericana]].<ref name="regulations">{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/sites/default/files/reglamento_conmebol_libertadores_bridgestone_2017_19_01_17_0.pdf |title=Reglamento Conmebol Libertadores Bridgestone 2017 |publisher=CONMEBOL.com |language=es}}</ref> They also automatically qualified for the [[2018 Copa Libertadores]] group stage. 

[[Grêmio Foot-Ball Porto Alegrense|Grêmio]] defeated [[Club Atlético Lanús|Lanús]] 3–1 on aggregate to win their third Copa Libertadores title.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/news/y=2017/m=11/news=gremio-set-for-world-stage-after-ending-continental-drought-2921949.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171130054505/http://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/news/y=2017/m=11/news=gremio-set-for-world-stage-after-ending-continental-drought-2921949.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 30, 2017|title=Gremio set for world stage after ending continental drought|publisher=FIFA.com|date=30 November 2017}}</ref>

==Format==
<section begin=Format />
The finals were played on a home-and-away [[two-legged tie|two-legged]] basis, with the higher-seeded team hosting the second leg. If tied on aggregate, the [[away goals rule]] would not be used, and 30 minutes of [[extra time (association football)|extra time]] would be played. If still tied after extra time, the [[penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] would be used to determine the winner.<ref name="regulations"/> If extra time was played, a fourth substitution would be allowed.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/es/se-podra-realizar-el-4to-cambio-en-caso-de-alargue |title=Se podrá realizar el 4to cambio en caso de alargue |publisher=CONMEBOL.com |language=es |date=29 November 2017}}</ref> <section end=Format />

==Matches==

===First leg===
[[Cícero Santos|Cícero]] scored the only goal in the 82nd minute with a left foot shot from six yards out after Jael headed the ball on to him inside the penalty box.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/es/gremio-toma-ventaja-en-el-primer-duelo-final-por-la-gloria-eterna |title=Gremio toma ventaja en el primer duelo final por la Gloria Eterna |publisher=CONMEBOL.com |language=es |date=22 November 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/2017/11/22/gremio-beats-lanus-in-first-leg-of-copa-libertadores-final/107951752/ |title=Gremio beats Lanus in first leg of Copa Libertadores final |date=22 November 2017 |publisher=USA Today.com}}</ref>

===Second leg===
Diego Braghieri (Lanús) and Walter Kannemann (Grêmio) missed the second leg after picking up a yellow card in the first leg.

Grêmio scored twice before half-time. [[Fernandinho (footballer, born November 1985)|Fernandinho]] stole the ball in Gremio's half, ran freely toward Andrada's goal and hammered it home from the edge of the box in the 26th minute. In the end of the first half, [[Luan Vieira|Luan]] dribbled through two Lanus defenders and lobbied the ball gently into the net. In the second half, [[José Sand]] scored from the penalty spot in the 71st minute.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/es/gremio-campeon-de-la-conmebol-libertadores-bridgestone-2017 |title=Gremio campeón de la CONMEBOL Libertadores Bridgestone 2017 |date=29 November 2017 |publisher=CONMEBOL.com |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.miamiherald.com/sports/article187235403.html |title=Brazil's Gremio wins Copa Libertadores for the 3rd time |date=29 November 2017 |publisher=Miami Herald.com |access-date=30 November 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201030459/http://www.miamiherald.com/sports/article187235403.html |archive-date=1 December 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
